# sinter

> sinter binds JSON APIs to plain HTML: keyed resources cached from the server, kept current from server events, rendered through <template> bindings, with optimistic mutations. A build step compiles annotated HTML into a page module; the browser runs no parser and no eval.

Package: @tiaforge-ui/sinter. Every directive is a `data-sn-*` attribute or an `<sn-*>` element. Anything else is a build error with a suggestion.

## Attributes

- `data-sn-state` (object literal): declares local reactive state for the element and its subtree
- `data-sn-let` (object literal {name: expression}): derived names for the element and its subtree, computed where they are read; later names may use earlier ones
- `data-sn-text` (value expression): sets textContent; never HTML
- `data-sn-attr` (object literal {href: …}): literal keys; null/false removes, true sets empty; URL values are checked; checked, selected, indeterminate and value also set the live property
- `data-sn-class` (object literal {unread: …}): toggles each class
- `data-sn-style` (object literal {'--color': …}): sets each property with style.setProperty
- `data-sn-show` (value expression): toggles the hidden attribute
- `data-sn-prefetch` (off): on <html>: no other page prefetches this one's data or the page itself (Speculation Rules), and none prerenders it; for pages that do something when they load
- `data-sn-transition` (value expression (a name)): the same thing on two pages: following a link from the element (or its row) to a page with an element of the same name morphs one into the other (view transitions; back too)
- `data-sn-prop` (object literal): sets JS properties; custom elements only (one defined later gets them again through its setters). On a component's tag: its props, live and read-only
- `data-sn-component` (props type): on the <template> of a component file (src/components/<name>.html): the props it takes, a TypeScript type literal such as { article: Article; compact?: boolean }
- `data-sn-early` (off): on a component's tag (a use): this use is left out of the early script and renders when the page module runs (build-time constants are still in the HTML); for uses that may shift the layout when they render, to keep the early script small
- `data-sn-import` (lazy packages, comma-separated): loads packages of sinter({ lazy }) when the element is rendered (at takeover outside templates, when its branch or row first renders inside one), instead of on first call
- `data-sn-preload` (lazy packages, comma-separated): the build preloads packages of sinter({ lazy }) with the page (<link rel="modulepreload"> in its head): fetched in parallel with the page bundle, run on first call or by data-sn-import
- `data-sn-ref` (name): in a component's markup: the element its script reads as this.refs.<name>, typed by its tag
- `data-sn-layout` (props type): on the <html> of a layout file (src/layouts/<name>.html): the props it takes; a page that is only the layout's tag fills its slots, in the head and the body
- `data-sn-head` (props type): on the <template> of a head component (src/components/<name>.html): its props, as data-sn-component; it holds any number of head elements (<title>, <meta>, <link>, …), inlined at its use in a head
- `data-sn-emits` (events type): on the <template data-sn-component>: the events emit() sends and their detail types, e.g. { select: Article }
- `data-sn-model` (state path | $url.<param>): two-way binding for form controls; on $url, the URL follows (a history entry; typing at each pause), and a <select multiple> or a checkbox with a value makes the parameter a list
- `data-sn-for` (item in list | (item, i) in list): repeats a <template> per item
- `data-sn-key` (value expression): row identity; defaults to the resource key or object identity
- `data-sn-reserve` (off | number of rows): on a <template data-sn-for> outside templates: builds hold the space this many rows take (a paginated resource: its page-size, without the attribute) until the data arrives, from the sizes the stylesheets give; off: no space held and no SN520
- `data-sn-if` (value expression): renders a <template> while truthy
- `data-sn-else`: on a <template> directly after an if template
- `data-sn-listbox` (id of the suggestion list, or empty): on a text input: arrow keys mark a [role=option] of that list (empty: the nearest [role=listbox] around the input), Enter or Tab clicks it, Escape fires `dismiss`
- `data-sn-persist` (storage key): persists the model or state in localStorage under sn:
- `data-sn-get` (URL template): GET action; latest wins
- `data-sn-post` (URL template): POST action
- `data-sn-put` (URL template): PUT action
- `data-sn-patch` (URL template): PATCH action
- `data-sn-delete` (URL template): DELETE action
- `data-sn-call` (action call): local action: calls a function from the actions module, e.g. pgp.decrypt(msg); a handler starts it with run('id')
- `data-sn-body` (value expression): JSON request body; overrides form serialization
- `data-sn-trigger` (DOM event name): overrides the default trigger
- `data-sn-debounce` (milliseconds): delays the trigger, resets on each event; without a method, delays the element's data-sn-on-* handlers
- `data-sn-concurrency` (block | queue | latest): mutations only; default block for forms, queue otherwise
- `data-sn-optimistic` (handler expression): patch/upsert/remove calls applied before the request, kept on success, rolled back on failure
- `data-sn-then` (handler expression): runs after a 2xx response; $result = parsed body
- `data-sn-catch` (handler expression): runs after an error; $error = {status, body, message, detail}. A form without it shows a 4xx `{errors: {name: message}}` on its fields (aria-invalid and the message); its markup reads the failure as `$error`
- `data-sn-confirm` (value expression): asks this question before the action runs (configure({ confirm }), window.confirm by default); no question when falsy
- `data-sn-encoding` (json | form): form: the body (data-sn-body, arrays as repeated keys, or the form) goes as application/x-www-form-urlencoded
- `data-sn-retry` (retry policy name): mutations only: sends the request again as that policy of configure({ retry }) says (after a network error, a 5xx, a 429), with an Idempotency-Key; without it a write is sent once
- `data-sn-apply` (off): turns write-through off for this mutation: its response is not applied to the resources it is about
- `data-sn-path` (URL patterns /a/:b …): on <html>: the path shapes this page is served for; `:name` segments appear read-only in $url
- `data-sn-data` (resource name): on <script type="application/json"> in <head>: initial data for a resource
- `data-sn-on-<event>` (handler expression): plain event handler, no request; e.g. data-sn-on-click
- `data-sn-on-keydown-<key>` (handler expression): runs only for that key (also on-keyup-<key>): modifiers first, the key last, e.g. data-sn-on-keydown-j, -shift-n (N), -mod-enter (Ctrl, Cmd on Apple), -escape, -question (?); matches KeyboardEvent.key; other Ctrl/Alt/Meta held do not match; an ancestor's filter skips keys typed into fields; a match calls preventDefault()
- `data-sn-debounce-<event>` (milliseconds): delays only that event's data-sn-on-<event> handler (it runs with the last event); e.g. data-sn-debounce-input

Key filters (`data-sn-on-keydown-<modifiers->key`, `data-sn-on-keyup-…`): modifiers `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`, `meta`, `mod`, then one key: `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `escape`, `enter`, `tab`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `insert`, `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, `arrowup`, `arrowdown`, `arrowleft`, `arrowright`, `contextmenu`, `f1`–`f12`, and characters by name: `slash` (`/`), `backslash` (`\`), `question` (`?`), `period` (`.`), `comma` (`,`), `semicolon` (`;`), `colon` (`:`), `quote` (`'`), `backquote` (``` ` ```), `minus` (`-`), `plus` (`+`), `equal` (`=`), `asterisk` (`*`), `bracketleft` (`[`), `bracketright` (`]`). Attribute names are lowercase, so N is `shift-n`; Shift is not checked for characters (`question` is ? however it is typed). Filters on an ancestor skip keys typed into fields (input, textarea, select, contenteditable) and Enter/Space on buttons and links; a filter on the field itself runs. A match calls `preventDefault()`; on one element, filters and a plain `data-sn-on-keydown` run in attribute order. The nearest element that handles an event wins: for clicks and other native events any handler or action that ran, for keys a matching filter, an action, a debounced handler, or a plain handler that called `$event.preventDefault()`; a key a plain handler does not prevent goes on to its ancestors, so a grid's arrow-key handler that prevents only the arrows leaves N to `<body data-sn-on-keydown-shift-n>`. Page-wide shortcuts go on `<body>`. Bubbling custom events (`emit()`, islands' `CustomEvent`s, `sn-error`, `dismiss`) are notifications: every element from the target up with a handler for one runs, inner first, until a handler calls `$event.preventDefault()` (the rest of that element's handlers and its action still run); `emit()` and `dismiss` are cancelable, and an island makes its events stoppable with `cancelable: true`. Debounced handlers and actions pass them on. A custom event that does not bubble, and a plain `Event`, go to the nearest element only. There is no `stop()`; `stopPropagation()` does not end the walk.

## Elements

- `<sn-resource>` `name`, `src`, `method`, `body`, `call`, `each`, `key`, `items`, `total`, `order`, `when`, `paginate`, `page-size`, `size-param`, `cursor`, `direction-param`, `direction-values`, `page-param`, `offset-param`, `page-model`, `type`, `cache`, `refresh`, `then`, `early`: a named, page-wide cache of server data; `cache` (or `cache="10m"`) shows the data from the last page load at once, then revalidates. `refresh="30s"` reloads it once that long has passed since its last load, whatever caused that load (server events, `refresh()`, a reconnect), in the background: `$meta.loading` stays false, and paused while the tab is hidden. `early="off"`: never preloaded or requested before the page module (for a resource whose request a middleware answers or changes). `then` is a handler run after each successful load (`$result`: what it loaded; the state around the resource in scope). With `sinter({ apis })`, `src` is a path relative to an API (`/articles`, `billing:/invoices`); `method="POST"` with `body` loads with a POST of that value. Loading needs no attributes: concurrent loads of one URL share a request, a `src` change aborts the running one (latest wins), a change typed into a text field waits 250 ms for the next keystroke, a resource only dialogs read is requested with low priority, and a bfcache restore or going back online refetches. `page-model="$url.page"` (offset lists) keeps the page in the URL: read at load, written back by page() (a history entry), followed when the URL changes
- `<sn-sync>` `src`: one server event stream
- `<sn-component>` `use`, `data-sn-prop`: a component chosen by data at runtime; `use` names it: ``use="`${b.type}-block`"`` (convention), `use="{ hero: 'hero-block' }[b.type]"` (map) or `use="blockComponent(b)"` (helper); it must fit `ComponentName`, every candidate must exist, props are checked per candidate (narrowed for convention and map); a value outside the candidates renders nothing, or the `data-sn-else` template after it
- `<sn-event>` `name`, `resource`, `op`, `item`, `set`, `when`, `fallback`, `then`, `type`: maps one server event to a change message; child of <sn-sync>. `then` is a handler run after the change (payload fields and the state around the sync in scope), e.g. close('detail'); with `then`, `resource` and `op` may be left out

## Expressions and scope

- Attribute values are JavaScript expressions, checked at build time. Value expressions (text, attr, class, show, for, if, key, body, state, URL interpolations) cannot assign, use `++`, `delete`, `await` or `import()`.
- Handlers (`data-sn-on-*`, `then`, `catch`) are statements separated by `;`: assignments to state, `$url.<param>` and `$locale`, and calls. No declarations or loops.
- `$url` is bindable: `data-sn-model="$url.q"` (a query parameter; path parameters are read-only), `page-model="$url.page"` on an offset list. History works as in a single-page app: a write a user's event caused (a click, a select, a checkbox, `page()`, an action's `then` it started) adds an entry; typing in a field bound to the URL commits at each 250 ms pause (the first commit of a run adds an entry, later ones replace it; Enter or leaving the field ends the run); other writes (a resource's `then`, a list's reset to page 1 after a filter change) replace; Back and Forward write nothing. Values are written as a reload reads them: numbers as strings, `true` as `'1'`, `false`/`null`/`''`/`[]` delete the parameter; use `+$url.page` for arithmetic. A parameter bound to a `<select multiple>` or checkboxes with a `value` is a list (repeated keys, `[]` when absent; test `$url.tag.length`, SN211). `page-model` makes the URL the list's single source: `page()` writes the page and the list follows; `$url.page` is the page asked for, `$meta.<name>.page` the page shown; a filter change starts at page 1. Guide: docs/navigation.md#the-url-and-the-history.
- A handler cannot call an action function (SN203). To start an action from a handler (a key filter, `data-sn-then`, `<sn-resource then>`), give the action element an `id` and call `run('id')`; the element's busy state, concurrency, optimistic layer and `then`/`catch` apply. A hidden carrier works: `<span hidden id="mark-read" data-sn-call="mail.markRead(open)"></span>`. See the recipe "Run an action from a handler".
- `then` on `<sn-event>` is a handler run after the event's change is applied: payload fields are bare names, the state around the `<sn-sync>` is in scope and assignable, and so are its `data-sn-let` names (read-only; state and lets win over payload fields of the same name), store functions work (`close('id')` names its dialog: there is no element). With `then`, `resource` and `op` may be left out.
- `then` on `<sn-resource>` is a handler run after each successful load (first load, `refresh()`, refetch events, `src` changes, every `page()`; per source for `each`), not for cached data shown at once, failed loads or optimistic/event changes. `$result` is what the load stored (what `items` selects; the page just loaded). The state around the resource is in scope and assignable; `close('id')` names its dialog. It runs on every refetch, so a once-only handler guards itself, one step per guard: `then="draft = $result ?? draft; $result && showModal('compose')"`.
- Server errors on a form: a mutation without `data-sn-catch` on a form, or on a button or control inside one, that fails with a 4xx and a JSON body `{errors: {<name>: message | message[]}}` marks each control with that `name`: `aria-invalid="true"` and the message in the element its `aria-errormessage` names, else in a `<small data-sn-error data-tone="danger">` inserted after it; the first such field gets focus; editing a field clears its error, sending again clears all. Inside the form, `$error` is its last failed send (`{status, body, message, detail}`, or `null`; null again when sent again): show the rest with bindings, e.g. `<template data-sn-if="$error"><p data-sn-text="$error.detail"></p></template>`. Shown (no `sn-error`, no `onError`) when every message marked a field or the form reads `$error`. `data-sn-catch` opts out. Another response format: `configure({ fieldErrors: (error, {url, method}) => ({ name: messages }) })` reading `error.body` (`null`: mark no field; `undefined`: the default reading); codes instead of text: map them to `m.key()` there.
- `refresh="30s"` on `<sn-resource>` reloads it in the background once its last load is that old, counted from every load (so a resource a stream keeps reloading rarely refreshes): `$meta.loading` stays false, nothing while the tab is hidden or `when` is falsy, failures back off up to 30 s and are reported once. A reload whose response has the `ETag` (else `Last-Modified`) of the data shown, unchanged since, is not stored or re-rendered, `then` still runs (on pages with `refresh` or `<sn-sync>`, which get the versions module); servers send `ETag` with `Cache-Control: no-cache` (and `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: ETag` cross-origin).
- `data-sn-optimistic` may only call `patch`, `upsert`, `remove`. The change shows at once, stays when the request succeeds (committed under what `then` writes) and is rolled back when it fails.
- A name resolves innermost first: loop variables, then the nearest `data-sn-state`, then resources, then magic names, helpers and store functions, then JavaScript globals. Browser APIs (`window`, `document`, `fetch`, timers, …) are refused: use a component's script.
- Resources are read-only: copy an item with `structuredClone(c)` to edit it, write with `patch()`.
- Helpers are plain function calls, never pipes: `date()`, `time()`, `datetime()`, `relative()`, `number()`, `bytes()`. Helper namespaces: `m.inbox_title()`.
- URL templates: `/api/x?id={c.id}`; interpolations are URL-encoded; the template must start with a literal `/path` or `https://origin`. A whole query value that is `null`/`undefined` or an empty array leaves the parameter out; an array is a repeated key (`?cal={cals}` → `cal=a&cal=b`); an array in the path is refused.
- Use `$now` instead of `Date.now()` so bindings update.

## Components

- A component is a file `src/components/<name>.html` (the name has a `-`), used as `<name>` on any page. It holds one `<template data-sn-component="{ article: Article; compact?: boolean }">` with exactly one root element, and optionally a `<style>`. `data-sn-emits="{ select: Article }"` on the template declares its events.
- Every use is expanded at build time: the root element replaces the tag, so the component renders in the first frame like page markup and needs no runtime. The caller's `class` is joined with the root's; other attributes, handlers (`data-sn-on-<event>`), actions, `data-sn-class`, `-attr`, `-style`, `-show` move onto the root in the caller's scope.
- Props go in with `data-sn-prop="{ article: a, compact: narrow }"`: each is the caller's expression, live and read-only. An optional prop not passed is `undefined`, or the root's `data-sn-state` field of the same name. The component sees only its props, its own state, resources, helpers and magic names; slot content (`<slot>`, `<slot name="meta">` with fallback content, filled by the caller's children and `slot="meta"`) sees the caller's scope.
- Events come out with `emit('select', article)` (names checked against `data-sn-emits`); the caller handles them with `data-sn-on-select`, `$event.detail` typed. `data-sn-model="draft.stars"` binds a component that declares a `value` prop and a `change` event.
- A component with a script: `src/components/<name>.ts` beside its HTML, `export class TaskRing extends TaskRingComponent` (imported from `./task-ring.html`, typed by the generated `src/sinter.components.d.ts`). sinter creates it per instance and calls `connected()` (markup rendered, refs set), `propsChanged()` and `disconnected()`; it reads `this.props`, writes `this.state` (renders), uses `this.refs.<name>` (`data-sn-ref` in its markup), `this.root` and `this.emit()`. It writes only state, never nodes sinter renders. Use it for browser work (canvas, libraries, timers) instead of a custom element.
- A component may use itself (a tree: comments and replies) when the inner use is inside a `data-sn-for` or `data-sn-if` template (else SN306): `<template data-sn-for="r in comment.replies" data-sn-key="r.id"><comment-thread data-sn-prop="{ comment: r }"></comment-thread></template>`. `patch(r, …)` and `remove(r)` change a nested item along its path at any depth; `upsert(comment.replies, x)` adds to a nested list. Nested loops need `data-sn-key`.
- `<sn-component use="`${b.type}-block`" data-sn-prop="{ block: b }">` picks a component per item: a template string, a map in the markup (`use="{ hero: 'hero-block' }[b.type]"`) or a helper; it must fit `ComponentName` (`b.type + '-block'` is a `string`: write the template string); a `data-sn-else` template after it renders for a value outside the candidates.
- `data-sn-early="off"` on a component's tag (`<tag-cloud data-sn-early="off">`) leaves that use out of the early script (smaller head script; it renders when the page module runs, so it may shift the layout then).
- `<sn-include>` is removed (SN316): a partial is a component.
- A head component is a file `src/components/<name>.html` with `<template data-sn-head="{ title?: string }">` instead of `data-sn-component`: it holds any number of head elements (`<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>`, `<script>`, `<style>`, `<noscript>`, `<base>`, `<template data-sn-if>`, slots, other head components), inlined at its use in a `<head>` with no wrapper. Its tag takes only `data-sn-prop` and slot content. A head component in a body, a component in a head, a body element in a head component: SN320.
- In a head, `<title data-sn-text>` binds, and a `<meta>` with a literal `name`, `property` or `itemprop` binds its `content`: `<meta name="description" content="Fallback" data-sn-attr="{ content: post?.summary ?? 'Fallback' }">`. Nothing else in a head binds (SN207). Constants are written into the HTML at build time; values from data render when it arrives, so scrapers that run no script see the literal content. A second `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`, `og:title`… in one head is SN321.
- A slot that is slot content of a component's tag forwards what fills it: `<seo-tags><slot name="seo" slot="extra"></slot></seo-tags>` puts the caller's `slot="seo"` content into `seo-tags`'s `extra` slot, in the caller's scope.

## Layouts

- A layout is a whole document `src/layouts/<name>.html` (the name has a `-`) whose `<html>` declares its props: `<!doctype html><html lang="en" data-sn-layout="{ title?: string; nav: string }"><head>…<slot name="head"></slot></head><body>…<slot></slot></body></html>`. It has any number of named slots in its head and body; the default slot is in the body (a default slot in the head: SN318). No script beside it, no `data-sn-emits`.
- A page that uses it is only its tag: `<site-layout data-sn-path="/post/:slug" data-sn-state="{ tab: 'all' }" data-sn-prop="{ nav: 'post', title: post?.title }">…</site-layout>` (anything else on the page, or the tag anywhere else: SN319). Children fill the slots; a head element goes to a head slot with `slot="head"` (a `<title>`/`<meta>`/`<link>` for a body slot: SN320). Plain attributes on the tag replace the layout's on `<html>` (`lang`, `dir`; `class` is joined); `data-sn-path` and `data-sn-prefetch` go onto `<html>`. Handlers on the tag are the page's `<body>` handlers (on the layout's `<body>`, ahead of its own): DOM events, `sn-error` and `dismiss` only (SN315), e.g. `data-sn-on-sn-error` and `data-sn-on-keydown-shift-n`.
- `data-sn-state` on the tag is the page's state: the props and all slot content see it, the layout's markup does not. The layout's markup sees its props, its own state, the page's resources and the globals.
- The merge happens before anything reads the page: early scripts, preloads, embedded data, Google Fonts and Vite's bundling of the layout's `<script type="module">` and stylesheets work on the merged document. Relative URLs in the layout (`./site.css`) are relative to the layout file. Layouts are not pages: leave `src/layouts/` out of the build's inputs (SN318).

## What belongs in markup

- Markup holds filters, conditions, single assignments and short calls. Logic goes into a helper when it computes a value (pure: unit-test it without a page), or into an action when it has side effects (`data-sn-call`).
- Handlers apply a helper's result to state: `data-sn-on-click="sel = rowClick($event, sel, f.id, ids)"`, not branches on `$event.shiftKey` in the attribute. See the row selection recipe.
- One step per condition: `open && close('detail')` is fine; `a && (b = null, close())` is not: split it into statements, let the dialog's `data-sn-on-close` reset state, or compute the new state in a helper.
- Warning SN507 (`complex-expression`) flags expressions that outgrew markup and names the limit: statements per handler (4), comma sequences (0), steps behind one `&&`/`||`/`?:` statement (1), `?:` nesting (2), operations in an arrow function (8), operations per expression (15). `sinter({ complexity: { …, level: 'warn' | 'error' | 'off' } })` changes them.

## Magic names

`$event`, `$el`, `$url`, `$now`, `$locale`, `$result`, `$error`, `$meta`. `$event` in handlers, `$result` in `then`, `$error` (`{status, body, message}`) in `catch`; `$meta.<resource>` has `loading`, `error`, `loadedAt`, `pending`, `total`, `live` (`'connecting'`, `'open'` or `'retrying'` for a resource a `<sn-sync>` event feeds, the worst of its streams; `null` otherwise), and with `paginate`: `page` (offset), `pages`, `from`, `to`, `hasPrev`, `hasNext`.

## Store functions

`refresh()`, `upsert()`, `patch()`, `remove()`, `page()`, `showModal()`, `close()`, `reset()`, `emit()`, `run()`: `refresh('name')` (or several: `refresh('a', 'b')`), `upsert('name', item)`, `patch(item, {…})`, `remove(item)` (no resource name: they act on the item in the resource it came from, found by key: a row of a `data-sn-for` over a resource, also through `filter`/`toSorted` or a helper given one resource; an element (`list[0]`, `.find(…)`); a single resource; a prop or emitted detail that is one; state assigned one, `sel = m` or `structuredClone(m)`; anything else is SN317), `page('name', 'next' | 'prev' | 'first' | 'last' | n)` (a page number needs offset mode or keyset with `offset-param`, else SN304; a computed direction such as `$event.shiftKey ? 'prev' : 'next'` works everywhere, typed by `sinter check`; `prev` does nothing while `hasPrev` is false and `next` while `hasNext` is false, in every mode, so paging needs no `$meta` guard; `first` and `last` always load), `showModal('id')` opens a dialog by its literal id, `close()` the nearest dialog or `close('id')` that one, `reset()` the nearest form, `emit('event', detail)` (a bubbling, cancelable `CustomEvent`), `run('id')` starts the action of the element with that literal id (SN311), as its trigger would but with `$event` null; a form is submitted (`requestSubmit()`, validation runs); a disabled or inert element does nothing; it returns nothing, results go to the element's `then`/`catch`. The resource name may be chosen from literals: `page(searching ? 'results' : 'messages', 'next')`, `||`/`??` between literals, or a `data-sn-let` name whose value is one (`data-sn-let="{ shown: searching ? 'results' : 'messages' }"`, then `page(shown, 'next')`, `$meta[shown].hasNext`); every name it can take is checked like a literal; a state variable or helper result is SN301 (make it a `?:`).

## Write-through

A mutation's 2xx response is applied to the store by itself, before `then` runs (the `apply` module, loaded when a page has something to apply). With an OpenAPI spec: an object of a named schema in the response (`{article: Article}`) patches the same-key item in every list of that schema and what the URL named (`{article.slug}` names the single `article`; `{article.author.username}` also names `article.author`, a Profile); a POST to exactly a list's current URL inserts the created item (the response's, else body + returned key, else a refetch; a filtered or paginated list is never inserted into); a PUT/PATCH body patches the entity the URL named. Without a spec: a DELETE of a row's URL (the list's URL plus one segment, from `c.id` with `c in comments`) removes the row, and a PUT/PATCH body patches the row when its keys are fields of the row. Patches merge and skip unchanged fields; `then` writes land on top. So `data-sn-then="patch(a, $result.article)"`, `upsert('comments', $result.comment)` and `remove(c)` are not written (SN510 says so); `data-sn-optimistic` is still how a change shows before the answer. `data-sn-apply="off"` turns it off for one element.

## Retries

Nothing is sent again unless a retry policy says so. Policies are named in the config module: `import { retry } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/retry'; configure({ sessionProbe: '/api/user', retry: retry({ policies: { drafts: { backoff: ['1s', '30s'] }, network: { backoff: ['1s', '10s'], retries: 3 } }, get: 'network' }) })` (fields: `backoff: [first, longest]`, `retries`, `maxAge`, `key`: the header, default `Idempotency-Key`, or `false`). A write opts in on its element: `data-sn-retry="drafts"` (mutations only; writes have no default). `get` is the policy of every GET except background refreshes. A network error waits, then the session probe decides (2xx: send again, 401: lost to the login redirect); a 5xx is a failed try; a 429 or 503 waits for `Retry-After` and fails at once when that is after the policy's last try; a retried DELETE that gets 404 succeeded; other 4xx fail at once. Each trigger sends one idempotency key on every try. A server that ignores the key may create a duplicate from a retried POST: create with a client id (`PUT /api/notes/{uuid}`). While a write waits, its element keeps `aria-busy` (show "not saved" with `body:has(form[aria-busy])`), its optimistic change stays, `latest` replaces it with a newer trigger (use it for drafts: `block` keeps a form disabled), and leaving the page asks first (not on iOS).

## Diagnostics

`SN101 unknown-attribute`, `SN102 wrong-element`, `SN103 missing-key`, `SN104 unsupported-model`, `SN201 unknown-identifier`, `SN202 forbidden-global`, `SN203 side-effect`, `SN204 optimistic-scope`, `SN205 resource-mutation`, `SN206 unknown-namespace-member`, `SN207 unsafe-sink`, `SN208 type-error`, `SN209 name-conflict`, `SN210 url-list-mismatch`, `SN211 url-list-condition`, `SN212 url-object-value`, `SN301 unknown-resource`, `SN302 duplicate-resource`, `SN303 unknown-meta-field`, `SN304 keyset-jump`, `SN306 component-cycle`, `SN307 openapi-invalid`, `SN308 unknown-schema-field`, `SN309 unknown-dialog`, `SN310 unknown-action`, `SN311 unknown-run-target`, `SN312 invalid-component`, `SN313 unknown-prop`, `SN314 unknown-slot`, `SN315 unknown-component-event`, `SN316 include-removed`, `SN317 no-item-source`, `SN318 invalid-layout`, `SN319 layout-use`, `SN320 head-content`, `SN321 duplicate-head`, `SN322 ships-javascript`, `SN323 needs-site`, `SN324 lazy-package-use`, `SN325 lazy-package-bundled`, `SN326 unknown-operation`, `SN327 undeclared-query`, `SN328 absolute-url`, `SN329 api-config`, `SN330 configured-shape`, `SN401 parse-error`, `SN501 unused-resource`, `SN502 non-reactive-value`, `SN503 data-bound-id`, `SN504 untyped-resource`, `SN505 unknown-query-param`, `SN506 untyped-event`, `SN507 complex-expression`, `SN509 run-cycle`, `SN510 redundant-write`, `SN511 image-too-small`, `SN512 image-stretched`, `SN513 bound-local-image`, `SN514 auto-fit-rows`, `SN515 redundant-path`, `SN516 unfed-live`, `SN517 unkeyed-list`, `SN518 redundant-shape`, `SN519 dropped-query`, `SN520 content-sized-list`.

## Recipes

Each recipe comes with its test; copy both.

### List with filter

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" items="people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<section data-sn-state="{ q: '' }">
  <input type="search" placeholder="Search" data-sn-model="q">
  <p data-sn-show="$meta.people.loading" aria-busy="true">Loading…</p>
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people.filter(p => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q.toLowerCase()))">
      <li data-sn-text="p.name"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
</section>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './list-filter.html?raw';


test('filters the list as you type', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/people': { people: [{ id: 1, name: 'Bob' }, { id: 2, name: 'Ada' }] } });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Ada', 'Bob']);

  const input = root.querySelector('input')!;
  input.value = 'ad';
  input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
  await flush();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Ada']);
});
```

### Form dialog with repeatable fields

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<section data-sn-state="{ draft: null }">
  <button data-sn-on-click="draft = {name: '', emails: [{value: ''}]}" commandfor="edit" command="show-modal">New</button>
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people">
      <li>
        <span data-sn-text="p.name"></span>
        <button data-sn-on-click="draft = structuredClone(p)" commandfor="edit" command="show-modal">Edit</button>
      </li>
    </template>
  </ul>

  <dialog id="edit">
    <form data-sn-post="/api/people" data-sn-body="draft"
          data-sn-then="upsert('people', $result); draft = null; close()"
          data-sn-catch="emit('toast', $error.message)">
      <input data-sn-model="draft.name" required>
      <template data-sn-for="(e, i) in draft.emails">
        <input type="email" data-sn-model="draft.emails[i].value">
      </template>
      <button type="button" data-sn-on-click="draft.emails.push({value: ''})">Add email</button>
      <button type="submit">Save</button>
    </form>
  </dialog>
</section>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './form-dialog.html?raw';


test('saves the draft and upserts the result', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/people': [],
    'POST /api/people': (call) => ({ id: 1, ...(call.body as object) }),
  });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();               // New
  const dialog = root.querySelector('dialog')!;
  dialog.showModal();
  dialog.dispatchEvent(new Event('toggle'));
  await flush();

  const [name, email] = root.querySelectorAll('dialog input');
  (name as HTMLInputElement).value = 'Ada';
  name!.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
  (email as HTMLInputElement).value = 'ada@example.com';
  email!.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
  root.querySelector('form')!.requestSubmit();
  await settle();

  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)!.body).toEqual({ name: 'Ada', emails: [{ value: 'ada@example.com' }] });
  expect(root.querySelector('li span')!.textContent).toBe('Ada');
  expect(dialog.open).toBe(false);
});
```

### Server validation errors on the fields

```html
<!-- Server validation errors: no data-sn-catch, so a 4xx with {errors: {email: "…"}} marks the field
     aria-invalid and shows the message after it (temper styles aria-invalid); `aria-errormessage`
     puts a message where you want it. Inside the form, `$error` is its last failed send: here a
     line for a failure that is not about a field (a 5xx). -->
<form data-sn-post="/api/signup" data-sn-then="emit('signed-up', $result)">
  <p data-tone="danger" data-sn-show="$error && !$error.body?.errors" data-sn-text="$error?.detail ?? $error?.message"></p>
  <label>Email <input type="email" name="email" required></label>
  <label>Username <input name="username" required aria-errormessage="username-error"></label>
  <small id="username-error" hidden></small>
  <button>Sign up</button>
</form>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './field-errors.html?raw';


test('shows the server\'s field errors on the fields', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'POST /api/signup': { status: 422, body: { errors: { email: 'is already taken', username: ['is too short'] } } },
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  const [email, username] = root.querySelectorAll('input');
  email!.value = 'ada@example.com';
  username!.value = 'a';
  root.querySelector('form')!.requestSubmit();
  await settle();

  expect(email!.getAttribute('aria-invalid')).toBe('true');
  expect(email!.nextElementSibling!.textContent).toBe('is already taken');
  expect(username!.getAttribute('aria-invalid')).toBe('true');
  expect(root.querySelector('#username-error')!.textContent).toBe('is too short');

  email!.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));   // editing clears that field's error
  expect(email!.hasAttribute('aria-invalid')).toBe(false);
});

test('shows a failure that is not about a field through $error', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'POST /api/signup': { status: 503, body: { message: 'Sign-ups are paused.' } } });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  for (const input of root.querySelectorAll('input')) input.value = 'ada@example.com';
  root.querySelector('form')!.requestSubmit();
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toBe('Sign-ups are paused.');
});
```

### SSE sync

```html
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<main data-sn-state="{ sel: null }">
  <sn-sync src="/api/events">
    <sn-event name="person_updated" resource="people" op="upsert" item="person" fallback="refetch"></sn-event>
    <!-- after the removal: close the dialog if it shows that person (closing clears `sel`) -->
    <sn-event name="person_removed" resource="people" op="remove"
              then="sel?.id === id && close('person')"></sn-event>
  </sn-sync>

  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="p in people">
      <li><button data-sn-on-click="sel = p; showModal('person')" data-sn-text="p.name"></button></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <dialog id="person" data-sn-on-close="sel = null"><h2 data-sn-text="sel?.name"></h2></dialog>
</main>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests, mockStream } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './sse-sync.html?raw';


test('applies server events to the list', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/people': [{ id: 1, name: 'Bob' }] });
  const stream = mockStream();
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests, streams: { '/api/events': stream } });
  await settle();

  stream.emit('person_updated', { person: { id: 2, name: 'Ada' } });
  stream.emit('person_removed', { id: 1 });
  await flush();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Ada']);
});

test('a removed person closes the dialog that shows them', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/people': [{ id: 1, name: 'Bob' }, { id: 2, name: 'Ada' }] });
  const stream = mockStream();
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests, streams: { '/api/events': stream } });
  await settle();
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();   // Ada
  await flush();
  const dialog = root.querySelector('dialog')!;
  expect(dialog.open).toBe(true);

  stream.emit('person_removed', { id: 1 });
  await flush();
  expect(dialog.open).toBe(true);
  stream.emit('person_removed', { id: 2 });
  await flush();
  expect(dialog.open).toBe(false);
});
```

### Optimistic toggle

```html
<sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" key="id"></sn-resource>

<template data-sn-for="m in messages">
  <article>
    <span data-sn-text="m.subject"></span>
    <button data-sn-patch="/api/messages/{m.id}"
            data-sn-body="{is_flagged: !m.is_flagged}"
            data-sn-optimistic="patch(m, {is_flagged: !m.is_flagged})"
            data-sn-attr="{'aria-pressed': m.is_flagged ? 'true' : 'false'}">★</button>
  </article>
</template>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './optimistic-toggle.html?raw';


test('flags at once and rolls back when the server refuses', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': [{ id: 1, subject: 'Hi', is_flagged: false }],
    'PATCH /api/messages/1': { status: 500 },
  });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const star = root.querySelector('button')!;

  star.click();
  await flush();
  expect(star.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('true');   // optimistic

  await settle();
  expect(star.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('false');  // rolled back
});

test('keeps the flag when the server accepts it', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': [{ id: 1, subject: 'Hi', is_flagged: false }],
    'PATCH /api/messages/1': null,
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const star = root.querySelector('button')!;

  star.click();
  await settle();
  expect(star.getAttribute('aria-pressed')).toBe('true');   // committed: no flip back
});
```

### Offline drafts: sent again once the connection is back

```html
<!-- src/sinter.config.js:
  import { configure } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter';
  import { retry } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/retry';
  configure({ sessionProbe: '/api/user', retry: retry({ policies: { drafts: { backoff: ['1s', '30s'] } } }) });
-->
<sn-resource name="note" src="/api/notes/7"></sn-resource>

<main data-sn-state="{ draft: { title: '', body: '' } }">
  <!-- latest: after reconnecting only the newest draft is sent; the form stays editable -->
  <form data-sn-put="/api/notes/7" data-sn-retry="drafts" data-sn-concurrency="latest"
        data-sn-trigger="input" data-sn-debounce="500"
        data-sn-optimistic="patch(note, draft)">
    <input name="title" data-sn-model="draft.title">
    <textarea name="body" data-sn-model="draft.body"></textarea>
  </form>
  <p class="unsaved">Not saved yet: it is sent again once the connection is back.</p>
</main>

<style>
  .unsaved { display: none; }
  body:has(form[aria-busy]) .unsaved { display: block; }
</style>
```

```ts
import { afterEach, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { configure } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter';
import { retry } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/retry';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './offline-draft.html?raw';

afterEach(() => configure({ sessionProbe: null, retry: null }));

test('a draft typed while offline is sent once the connection is back, with one key', async () => {
  configure({ sessionProbe: '/api/user', retry: retry({ policies: { drafts: { backoff: ['1s', '30s'] } } }) });
  let online = false;
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/notes/7': { id: 7, title: 'Plan', body: '' },
    'GET /api/user': () => (online ? { name: 'me' } : { status: 503 }),
    'PUT /api/notes/7': (c) => { if (!online) throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch'); return c.body; },
  });
  const { root, settle, advance } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const form = root.querySelector('form')!, title = root.querySelector('input')!;

  title.value = 'Plan for Monday';
  title.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
  await advance(500);    // the debounce
  await settle();
  expect(form.getAttribute('aria-busy')).toBe('true');   // waiting: "Not saved yet" shows

  await advance(1000);   // the probe fails (offline): wait longer
  await settle();
  online = true;
  await advance(2000);   // the probe answers: sent again
  await settle();
  const puts = requests.calls.filter((c) => c.method === 'PUT');
  expect(puts).toHaveLength(2);
  expect(puts[1]!.body).toEqual({ title: 'Plan for Monday', body: '' });
  expect(puts[1]!.headers['idempotency-key']).toBe(puts[0]!.headers['idempotency-key']);
  expect(form.hasAttribute('aria-busy')).toBe(false);
});
```

### Pagination

```html
<sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" items="messages" total="total" key="id"
  paginate="keyset" page-size="2" cursor="{before: id}"></sn-resource>

<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="m in messages"><li data-sn-text="m.subject"></li></template>
</ul>
<nav>
  <button data-sn-on-click="page('messages', 'prev')" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !$meta.messages.hasPrev}">‹</button>
  <span data-sn-text="`${$meta.messages.from}–${$meta.messages.to} of ${$meta.messages.total}`"></span>
  <button data-sn-on-click="page('messages', 'next')" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !$meta.messages.hasNext}">›</button>
</nav>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './pagination.html?raw';

const all = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1].map((id) => ({ id, subject: `m${id}` }));

test('moves to the next page with a cursor', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': (call) => {
      const q = new URL(call.url, 'http://x').searchParams;
      const before = Number(q.get('before') ?? Infinity);
      const items = q.get('direction') === 'next' ? all.filter((m) => m.id < before) : all;
      return { messages: items.slice(0, Number(q.get('limit'))), total: all.length };
    },
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('span')!.textContent).toBe('1–2 of 5');

  root.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('nav button:last-of-type')!.click();
  await settle();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['m3', 'm2']);
  expect(root.querySelector('span')!.textContent).toBe('3–4 of 5');
  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)!.url).toBe('/api/messages?before=4&limit=2&direction=next');
});
```

### Pagination in the URL: page-model, shared links and Back

```html
<!-- The page lives in the URL: ?page=3 is read at load and written back on every move. -->
<sn-resource name="articles" src="/api/articles" items="articles" total="count" key="slug"
  paginate="offset" page-size="2" offset-param="offset" page-model="$url.page"></sn-resource>

<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="a in articles"><li data-sn-text="a.title"></li></template>
</ul>
<nav>
  <button data-sn-on-click="page('articles', 'prev')" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !$meta.articles.hasPrev}">‹</button>
  <template data-sn-for="n in Array.from({ length: $meta.articles.pages ?? 0 }, (_, i) => i + 1)" data-sn-key="n">
    <!-- the active link reads the page asked for ($url.page); the range below, the page shown ($meta) -->
    <button data-sn-on-click="page('articles', n)" data-sn-class="{active: n == (+$url.page || 1)}" data-sn-text="n"></button>
  </template>
  <button data-sn-on-click="page('articles', 'next')" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !$meta.articles.hasNext}">›</button>
  <span data-sn-text="`${$meta.articles.from}–${$meta.articles.to} of ${$meta.articles.total}`"></span>
</nav>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './url-pagination.html?raw';

const all = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((n) => ({ slug: `a${n}`, title: `A${n}` }));
const api = () => mockRequests({
  'GET /api/articles': (call) => {
    const q = new URL(call.url, 'http://x').searchParams, o = Number(q.get('offset')), n = Number(q.get('limit'));
    return { articles: all.slice(o, o + n), count: all.length };
  },
});
const titles = (root: HTMLElement) => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent);

test('a shared link opens its page; moving writes the URL; Back goes to the page before', async () => {
  const { root, settle, url, back } = await render(page, { requests: api(), url: 'http://localhost/?page=2' });
  await settle();
  expect(titles(root)).toEqual(['A3', 'A4']);
  root.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('nav > button:last-of-type')!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(url()).toBe('http://localhost/?page=3');
  expect(titles(root)).toEqual(['A5']);
  expect(root.querySelector('.active')!.textContent).toBe('3');
  await back();
  await settle();
  expect(titles(root)).toEqual(['A3', 'A4']);
});
```

### Search in the URL: a model on $url, one history entry per search

```html
<!-- A search field bound to the URL: one history entry per search, the request and the URL wait
     for the typing pause; a reload or a shared link shows the same results. -->
<sn-resource name="hits" src="/api/search?q={$url.q}&sort={$url.sort}" items="hits" key="id"
  when="$url.q"></sn-resource>

<input type="search" placeholder="Search" data-sn-model="$url.q">
<select data-sn-model="$url.sort">
  <option value="">Best match</option>
  <option value="new">Newest</option>
</select>
<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="h in hits"><li data-sn-text="h.title"></li></template>
</ul>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './url-search.html?raw';

const api = () => mockRequests({
  'GET /api/search': (call) => {
    const q = new URL(call.url, 'http://x').searchParams;
    return { hits: [{ id: 1, title: `${q.get('q')} (${q.get('sort') || 'best'})` }] };
  },
});
const type = (el: HTMLInputElement, v: string) => { el.value = v; el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); };

test('typing writes the URL once per pause; a select is an entry of its own; a shared link restores both', async () => {
  const requests = api();
  const { root, settle, flush, history } = await render(page, { requests });
  const field = root.querySelector('input')!;
  for (const v of ['s', 'si', 'sinter']) { type(field, v); await flush(); }
  await settle();
  expect(history()).toEqual(['http://localhost/', 'http://localhost/?q=sinter']);
  expect(requests.calls.map((c) => c.url)).toEqual(['/api/search?q=sinter']);
  const sort = root.querySelector('select')!;
  sort.value = 'new'; sort.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));
  await settle();
  expect(history()).toEqual(['http://localhost/', 'http://localhost/?q=sinter', 'http://localhost/?q=sinter&sort=new']);

  const shared = await render(page, { requests: api(), url: 'http://localhost/?q=sinter&sort=new' });
  await shared.settle();
  expect(shared.root.querySelector('input')!.value).toBe('sinter');
  expect(shared.root.querySelector('li')!.textContent).toBe('sinter (new)');
});
```

### A multi-select filter in the URL: an array parameter

```html
<!-- A multi-select filter in the URL: checkboxes with a `value` make `$url.tag` a list, written as
     repeated keys (?tag=go&tag=rust) and sent the same way. -->
<sn-resource name="posts" src="/api/posts?tag={$url.tag}" items="posts" key="id"></sn-resource>

<fieldset>
  <label><input type="checkbox" value="go" data-sn-model="$url.tag"> Go</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" value="rust" data-sn-model="$url.tag"> Rust</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" value="ts" data-sn-model="$url.tag"> TypeScript</label>
  <!-- a list is always truthy: test its length -->
  <button data-sn-on-click="$url.tag = []" data-sn-show="$url.tag.length">Clear</button>
</fieldset>
<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="p in posts"><li data-sn-text="p.title"></li></template>
</ul>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './url-filter.html?raw';

const api = () => mockRequests({
  'GET /api/posts': (call) => ({ posts: new URL(call.url, 'http://x').searchParams.getAll('tag').map((t, i) => ({ id: i, title: t })) }),
});

test('each box is an entry; the tags go to the URL and the request as repeated keys; Clear removes them', async () => {
  const requests = api();
  const { root, settle, url, history } = await render(page, { requests, url: 'http://localhost/?tag=go' });
  await settle();
  const boxes = root.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('input');
  expect([...boxes].map((b) => b.checked)).toEqual([true, false, false]);
  boxes[1]!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(url()).toBe('http://localhost/?tag=go&tag=rust');
  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)!.url).toBe('/api/posts?tag=go&tag=rust');
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['go', 'rust']);
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(url()).toBe('http://localhost/');
  expect(root.querySelector('button')!.hidden).toBe(true);
  expect(history()).toHaveLength(3);
});
```

### SignalR (or another transport) for <sn-sync>

```html
<!-- The page is the same as with SSE: only the configured transport differs (signalr-transport.js). -->
<sn-resource name="people" src="/api/people" key="id" order="name"></sn-resource>

<sn-sync src="/hubs/people">
  <sn-event name="person_updated" resource="people" op="upsert" item="person"></sn-event>
  <sn-event name="person_removed" resource="people" op="remove"></sn-event>
</sn-sync>

<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="p in people"><li data-sn-text="p.name"></li></template>
</ul>
```

```js
// SignalR transport for <sn-sync>, in your app (sinter does not depend on @microsoft/signalr).
// In src/sinter.config.js:
//
//   import { HubConnectionBuilder } from '@microsoft/signalr';
//   import { configure } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter';
//   import { signalRTransport } from './signalr-transport.js';
//
//   configure({
//     transport: (url) => url.startsWith('/hubs/')
//       ? signalRTransport(() => new HubConnectionBuilder().withUrl(url).build())
//       : undefined,
//   });
//
// Server: `await Clients.All.SendAsync("person_updated", new { person })`; the first argument is
// the payload. Hub method names are case-insensitive in SignalR, so keep event names distinct in
// more than case. Do not call withAutomaticReconnect(): sinter reconnects (session probe, backoff,
// refetch of everything the stream feeds), and two reconnect loops would race. Auth is the hub's:
// cookies, or withUrl(url, { accessTokenFactory }); request middleware does not apply.

/** @param {() => import('@microsoft/signalr').HubConnection} build a new, unstarted connection */
export function signalRTransport(build) {
  let hub = null;
  let deliver = null;
  const names = new Set();
  const add = (name) => {
    if (!hub || names.has(name)) return;
    names.add(name);
    const h = hub;
    h.on(name, (payload) => { if (hub === h) deliver(name, payload ?? null); });
  };
  return {
    connect(url, onEvent, onState, initial) {
      const h = hub = build();
      deliver = onEvent;
      names.clear();
      for (const n of initial) add(n);
      h.onclose(() => { if (hub === h) { hub = null; onState('error'); } });
      h.start().then(() => { if (hub === h) onState('open'); }, () => { if (hub === h) { hub = null; onState('error'); } });
    },
    listen: add,
    close() {
      const h = hub;
      hub = null; // nothing is reported after close()
      h?.stop().catch(() => {});
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import { afterEach, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { configure } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import { signalRTransport } from './signalr-transport.js';
import page from './signalr.html?raw';

// A stand-in for HubConnection: the test calls invoke() where the server would call SendAsync().
function fakeHub() {
  const handlers = new Map<string, (payload: unknown) => void>();
  let onclose = () => {};
  return {
    started: false,
    on(name: string, fn: (payload: unknown) => void) { handlers.set(name, fn); },
    onclose(fn: () => void) { onclose = fn; },
    async start() { this.started = true; },
    async stop() { this.started = false; },
    invoke(name: string, payload: unknown) { handlers.get(name)?.(payload); },
    lose() { this.started = false; onclose(); },
  };
}

afterEach(() => configure({ transport: null }));

test('applies hub messages to the list', async () => {
  const hubs: Array<ReturnType<typeof fakeHub>> = [];
  configure({ transport: (url) => (url.startsWith('/hubs/') ? signalRTransport(() => { hubs.push(fakeHub()); return hubs.at(-1) as never; }) : undefined) });
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/people': [{ id: 1, name: 'Bob' }] });
  const { root, flush, settle, advance } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  expect(hubs[0]!.started).toBe(true);

  hubs[0]!.invoke('person_updated', { person: { id: 2, name: 'Ada' } });
  hubs[0]!.invoke('person_removed', { id: 1 });
  await flush();
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Ada']);

  // a lost connection: sinter reconnects with a new hub and refetches what the stream feeds
  hubs[0]!.lose();
  await advance(2000); // the backoff (1 s ± jitter) before reconnecting
  await settle();
  expect(hubs).toHaveLength(2);
  expect(requests.calls.filter((c) => c.path === '/api/people')).toHaveLength(2);
});
```
