### Cached list across page loads

```html
<!-- `cache`: the next page load shows this list at once, then revalidates.
     `$meta.inbox.loading` with data present means "updating"; `$meta.inbox.loadedAt`
     stays null until the server has answered on this page. -->
<sn-resource name="inbox" src="/api/messages?folder=inbox" key="id" order="-date" cache="1h"></sn-resource>

<p data-sn-show="$meta.inbox.loading && inbox.length">Updating…</p>
<ul>
  <template data-sn-for="m in inbox">
    <li data-sn-text="m.subject"></li>
  </template>
</ul>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests, memoryStorage } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './cached-list.html?raw';

const subjects = (root: HTMLElement) => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent);

test('the next page load shows the cached list while it revalidates', async () => {
  // one tab: the same sessionStorage for both page loads
  const session = memoryStorage();
  const first = await render(page, { session, requests: mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': [{ id: 1, subject: 'Welcome', date: '2026-01-01' }],
  }) });
  await first.settle();

  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { session, requests: mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': [{ id: 2, subject: 'Lunch?', date: '2026-01-02' }, { id: 1, subject: 'Welcome', date: '2026-01-01' }],
  }) });
  expect(subjects(root)).toEqual(['Welcome']);                    // cached, before any response
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.hidden).toBe(false);            // "Updating…"

  await settle();
  expect(subjects(root)).toEqual(['Lunch?', 'Welcome']);
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.hidden).toBe(true);
});
```

### Local actions: hash a file, then upload it

```html
<section data-sn-state="{ file: null, url: '', error: '' }">
  <sn-resource name="digest" call="sha256(file)" when="file"></sn-resource>

  <input type="file" data-sn-on-change="file = $el.files[0] ?? null; url = ''">
  <p data-sn-show="$meta.digest.loading">Hashing…</p>
  <code data-sn-text="digest"></code>

  <button data-sn-call="upload(file, digest)" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !digest}"
          data-sn-then="url = $result.url; error = ''" data-sn-catch="error = $error.message">Upload</button>
  <a data-sn-show="url" data-sn-attr="{href: url}">Uploaded</a>
  <p role="alert" data-sn-text="error"></p>
</section>
```

```js
// src/sinter.actions.js: functions pages call with data-sn-call and <sn-resource call>.
// The last argument is sinter's context; with JSDoc types, `sinter check` checks the calls.
/** @import { CallContext } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter' */

/**
 * The file's SHA-256 as hex; choosing another file aborts the running hash through ctx.signal.
 * @param {File} file
 * @param {CallContext} ctx
 * @returns {Promise<string>}
 */
export async function sha256(file, ctx) {
  const bytes = await file.arrayBuffer();
  ctx.signal.throwIfAborted();
  const hash = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', bytes);
  return [...new Uint8Array(hash)].map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}

/**
 * ctx.request goes through the app's middleware (headers, 401 handling, allowed origins).
 * @param {File} file
 * @param {string} digest
 * @param {CallContext} ctx
 * @returns {Promise<{ url: string }>}
 */
export async function upload(file, digest, ctx) {
  const form = new FormData();
  form.append('file', file);
  form.append('sha256', digest);
  return /** @type {Promise<{ url: string }>} */ (ctx.request('/api/uploads', { method: 'POST', body: form }));
}
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { checkPage } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/check';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import * as actions from './local-actions.actions.js';
import source from './local-actions.actions.js?raw';
import page from './local-actions.html?raw';

const DIGEST = 'ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad'; // sha256('abc')

function choose(input: HTMLInputElement, file: File) {
  Object.defineProperty(input, 'files', { value: [file], configurable: true });
  input.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));
}

test('hashes the chosen file, then uploads it with its digest', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'POST /api/uploads': { url: '/files/1' } });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { actions, requests });
  const button = root.querySelector('button')!;
  expect(button.disabled).toBe(true);

  choose(root.querySelector('input')!, new File(['abc'], 'abc.txt'));
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('code')!.textContent).toBe(DIGEST);
  expect(button.disabled).toBe(false);

  button.click();
  await settle();
  expect((requests.calls[0]!.body as FormData).get('sha256')).toBe(DIGEST);
  expect(root.querySelector('a')!.getAttribute('href')).toBe('/files/1');
});

test('a failed upload shows the server message', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'POST /api/uploads': { status: 413, body: { message: 'File too large' } } });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { actions, requests });
  choose(root.querySelector('input')!, new File(['abc'], 'abc.txt'));
  await settle();
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('[role=alert]')!.textContent).toBe('File too large');
});

test('sinter check: arguments are checked against the actions', () => {
  const files = { 'src/sinter.actions.js': source };
  expect(checkPage(page, { files })).toEqual([]);
  const [d] = checkPage(page.replace('upload(file, digest)', 'upload(file)'), { files });
  expect([d!.code, d!.message]).toEqual(['SN208', expect.stringContaining("is not assignable to type '[file: File, digest: string]'")]);
});
```

### Keyboard shortcuts

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
<body data-sn-state="{ cursor: 0, open: null, marked: [] }"
      data-sn-on-keydown-j="cursor = Math.min(cursor + 1, messages.length - 1)"
      data-sn-on-keydown-k="cursor = Math.max(cursor - 1, 0)"
      data-sn-on-keydown-enter="open = messages[cursor]"
      data-sn-on-keydown-escape="open = null"
      data-sn-on-keydown-ctrl-space="marked = marked.includes(cursor) ? marked.filter(i => i !== cursor) : [...marked, cursor]"
      data-sn-on-keydown-slash="$el.querySelector('input').focus()">
  <sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" items="messages" key="id"></sn-resource>
  <!-- in the field, j, k and / are typed; its own Escape filter leaves it -->
  <input type="search" placeholder="Search (/)" data-sn-on-keydown-escape="$el.blur()">
  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="(m, i) in messages">
      <li data-sn-class="{cursor: i === cursor, marked: marked.includes(i)}" data-sn-text="m.subject"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <article data-sn-show="open" data-sn-text="open && open.subject"></article>
</body>
</html>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './keyboard-shortcuts.html?raw';

const key = (el: Element, k: string, init: KeyboardEventInit = {}) =>
  el.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: k, bubbles: true, cancelable: true, ...init }));

test('j/k move the cursor, Ctrl+Space marks, Enter opens, Escape closes; keys typed in the search field stay there', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/messages': { messages: [{ id: 1, subject: 'Hello' }, { id: 2, subject: 'Lunch?' }] } });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const body = root /* the <body> */, rows = () => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')];
  key(body, 'j');
  key(body, ' ', { ctrlKey: true });
  key(body, 'Enter');
  await flush();
  expect(rows().map((li) => li.className)).toEqual(['', 'cursor marked']);
  expect(root.querySelector('article')!.textContent).toBe('Lunch?');

  key(root.querySelector('input')!, 'k');  // typing a k
  key(body, 'Escape');
  await flush();
  expect(rows()[1]!.className).toBe('cursor marked');
  expect(root.querySelector('article')!.hidden).toBe(true);

  key(body, '/');
  expect(root.ownerDocument.activeElement).toBe(root.querySelector('input'));
});
```

### Row selection with Ctrl and Shift: logic in a helper, applied by the handler

```html
<sn-resource name="files" src="/api/files" items="files" key="id"></sn-resource>

<!-- the logic is in rowClick() (row-select.helpers.js); the handler only applies its result -->
<section data-sn-state="{ sel: noSelection() }" data-sn-let="{ ids: files.map(f => f.id) }">
  <p data-sn-text="sel.keys.length + ' selected'"></p>
  <ul role="listbox" aria-multiselectable="true">
    <template data-sn-for="f in files">
      <li role="option" data-sn-attr="{'aria-selected': sel.keys.includes(f.id) ? 'true' : 'false'}"
          data-sn-on-click="sel = rowClick($event, sel, f.id, ids)" data-sn-text="f.name"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <button data-sn-show="sel.keys.length" data-sn-on-click="sel = noSelection()">Clear</button>
</section>
```

```js
// Helpers hold the logic; the page applies their result (`sel = rowClick(…)`).
// They are pure: the same arguments give the same result, nothing else is read or changed,
// so they are unit-tested without a page.

/** No row selected. */
export const noSelection = () => ({ keys: [], anchor: null });

/**
 * The selection after a click on the row `key`, as a file manager does it. `sel` is
 * `{ keys, anchor }`, `keys` the rows' keys in the order they are shown.
 * - a click selects only that row;
 * - Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) adds or removes that row;
 * - Shift selects the rows from the anchor (the last row clicked without Shift) to this one;
 *   with Ctrl too, it adds them to the selection.
 */
export function rowClick(event, sel, key, keys) {
  const add = event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey;
  if (event.shiftKey && sel.anchor != null && keys.includes(sel.anchor)) {
    const a = keys.indexOf(sel.anchor), b = keys.indexOf(key);
    const range = keys.slice(Math.min(a, b), Math.max(a, b) + 1);
    const chosen = new Set([...(add ? sel.keys : []), ...range]);
    return { keys: keys.filter((k) => chosen.has(k)), anchor: sel.anchor };
  }
  if (add) {
    const chosen = sel.keys.includes(key) ? sel.keys.filter((k) => k !== key) : [...sel.keys, key];
    return { keys: keys.filter((k) => chosen.includes(k)), anchor: key };
  }
  return { keys: [key], anchor: key };
}
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import * as helpers from './row-select.helpers.js';
import page from './row-select.html?raw';

const { rowClick, noSelection } = helpers;

// the helper: pure, so tested with plain values
describe('rowClick', () => {
  const keys = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'];
  const click = (init: Partial<MouseEvent> = {}) => ({ ctrlKey: false, metaKey: false, shiftKey: false, ...init }) as MouseEvent;
  test('a click selects only that row and makes it the anchor', () => {
    expect(rowClick(click(), { keys: ['a', 'c'], anchor: 'a' }, 'b', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['b'], anchor: 'b' });
  });
  test('Ctrl or Cmd adds or removes the row, in display order', () => {
    expect(rowClick(click({ ctrlKey: true }), { keys: ['c'], anchor: 'c' }, 'a', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['a', 'c'], anchor: 'a' });
    expect(rowClick(click({ metaKey: true }), { keys: ['a', 'c'], anchor: 'a' }, 'c', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['a'], anchor: 'c' });
  });
  test('Shift selects from the anchor, in either direction; with Ctrl it adds', () => {
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true }), { keys: ['b'], anchor: 'b' }, 'd', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['b', 'c', 'd'], anchor: 'b' });
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true }), { keys: ['c'], anchor: 'c' }, 'a', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['a', 'b', 'c'], anchor: 'c' });
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true, ctrlKey: true }), { keys: ['a', 'd'], anchor: 'd' }, 'c', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['a', 'c', 'd'], anchor: 'd' });
  });
  test('Shift without an anchor (or a removed one) is a plain click', () => {
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true }), noSelection(), 'c', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['c'], anchor: 'c' });
    expect(rowClick(click({ shiftKey: true }), { keys: ['x'], anchor: 'x' }, 'c', keys)).toEqual({ keys: ['c'], anchor: 'c' });
  });
});

// the page: the handler applies the helper's result
test('click, Ctrl+click and Shift+click select rows', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/files': { files: ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'].map((id) => ({ id, name: id.toUpperCase() })) } });
  const { root, flush, settle } = await render(page, { requests, helpers });
  await settle();
  const rows = () => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')];
  const click = (i: number, init: MouseEventInit = {}) => rows()[i]!.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', { bubbles: true, ...init }));
  const selected = () => rows().filter((li) => li.getAttribute('aria-selected') === 'true').map((li) => li.textContent);

  click(1);
  click(3, { shiftKey: true });
  await flush();
  expect(selected()).toEqual(['B', 'C', 'D']);
  click(0, { ctrlKey: true });
  await flush();
  expect(selected()).toEqual(['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']);
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toBe('4 selected');
  root.querySelector('button')!.click();
  await flush();
  expect(selected()).toEqual([]);
});
```

### Run an action from a handler: mark a mail read once its body has loaded, and a shortcut

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
<body data-sn-state="{ open: null, error: '' }" data-sn-on-keydown-e="run('archive')">
  <sn-resource name="messages" src="/api/messages" items="messages" key="id"></sn-resource>
  <!-- loads when a mail opens; once its body is there, an unread mail is marked read -->
  <sn-resource name="body" src="/api/messages/{open.id}/body" when="open"
               then="$result && !open.is_read && run('mark-read')"></sn-resource>

  <ul>
    <template data-sn-for="m in messages">
      <li data-sn-class="{unread: !m.is_read}" data-sn-on-click="open = m" data-sn-text="m.subject"></li>
    </template>
  </ul>
  <article data-sn-show="open" data-sn-text="body && body.text"></article>

  <!-- no visible control: the element only carries the action (data-sn-call works the same) -->
  <span hidden id="mark-read" data-sn-patch="/api/messages/{open.id}" data-sn-body="{is_read: true}"
        data-sn-optimistic="patch(open, {is_read: true})"
        data-sn-catch="error = $error.message"></span>
  <!-- the button and E run one action; while it is disabled, E does nothing either -->
  <button id="archive" data-sn-post="/api/messages/{open.id}/archive" data-sn-attr="{disabled: !open}"
          data-sn-optimistic="remove(open)" data-sn-then="open = null">Archive (E)</button>
  <p role="alert" data-sn-text="error"></p>
</body>
</html>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { checkPage } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/check';
import { render, mockRequests } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './run-action.html?raw';

const MESSAGES = { messages: [{ id: 1, subject: 'Hello', is_read: false }, { id: 2, subject: 'Lunch?', is_read: true }] };
const key = (el: Element, k: string) => el.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: k, bubbles: true, cancelable: true }));

test('opening an unread mail marks it read once its body has loaded; a read one sends nothing', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': MESSAGES,
    'GET /api/messages/1/body': { text: 'Hi there' },
    'GET /api/messages/2/body': { text: 'At noon?' },
    'PATCH /api/messages/1': null,
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  const rows = () => [...root.querySelectorAll('li')];
  expect(rows().map((li) => li.className)).toEqual(['unread', '']);

  rows()[0]!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('article')!.textContent).toBe('Hi there');
  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)).toMatchObject({ method: 'PATCH', path: '/api/messages/1', body: { is_read: true } });
  expect(rows()[0]!.className).toBe('');

  rows()[1]!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(requests.calls.filter((c) => c.method === 'PATCH')).toHaveLength(1);
});

test('a failed mark-read rolls back and shows the error', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': MESSAGES,
    'GET /api/messages/1/body': { text: 'Hi there' },
    'PATCH /api/messages/1': { status: 503, body: { message: 'Mail server unavailable' } },
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  root.querySelector('li')!.click();
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('li')!.className).toBe('unread');
  expect(root.querySelector('[role=alert]')!.textContent).toBe('Mail server unavailable');
});

test('E archives the open mail through the button; with no mail open the button is disabled and E does nothing', async () => {
  const requests = mockRequests({
    'GET /api/messages': MESSAGES,
    'GET /api/messages/2/body': { text: 'At noon?' },
    'POST /api/messages/2/archive': null,
  });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, { requests });
  await settle();
  key(root, 'e');
  await settle();
  expect(requests.calls.map((c) => c.method)).toEqual(['GET']);

  root.querySelectorAll('li')[1]!.click();
  await settle();
  key(root, 'e');
  await settle();
  expect(requests.calls.at(-1)).toMatchObject({ method: 'POST', path: '/api/messages/2/archive' });
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('li')].map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(['Hello']);
  expect(root.querySelector('button')!.disabled).toBe(true);
});

test('sinter check: run() names an element with an action', () => {
  expect(checkPage(page).filter((d) => d.severity === 'error')).toEqual([]);
  const [d] = checkPage(page.replace("run('mark-read')", "run('mark-raed')")).filter((x) => x.severity === 'error');
  expect([d!.code, d!.message]).toEqual(['SN311', 'no element `id="mark-raed"` on this page. Did you mean `mark-read`?']);
});
```

### First paint: page chrome that renders before the script

```html
<!-- First paint: what renders before the page module has run. Chrome stays outside data templates (or in a
     data-sn-if over state), so the early chunk renders it before the first paint: messages in the language
     picked before the paint, the current page from literal state, the persisted collapse. Only what needs
     data waits in a template for the page module. -->
<body data-sn-state="{ here: '/mail/' }">
  <sn-resource name="user" src="/api/user"></sn-resource>
  <nav data-sn-attr="{'aria-label': m.nav()}" data-sn-state="{ collapsed: false }">
    <input type="checkbox" data-sn-model="collapsed" data-sn-persist="nav-collapsed" data-sn-attr="{'aria-label': m.collapse()}">
    <a href="/mail/" data-sn-attr="{'aria-current': here === '/mail/' ? 'page' : null}"><span data-sn-text="m.mail()"></span></a>
    <a href="/calendar/" data-sn-attr="{'aria-current': here === '/calendar/' ? 'page' : null}"><span data-sn-text="m.calendar()"></span></a>
    <!-- needs the user: renders when the page module has loaded it -->
    <template data-sn-if="user"><span data-sn-text="user.name"></span></template>
  </nav>
</body>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { firstPaint, memoryStorage, mockRequests, render } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './first-paint.html?raw';

// the message files (see the Messages recipe)
const messages = {
  en: { nav: 'Main navigation', collapse: 'Collapse menu', mail: 'Mail', calendar: 'Calendar' },
  de: { nav: 'Hauptnavigation', collapse: 'Menü einklappen', mail: 'E-Mail', calendar: 'Kalender' },
};

test('before the page module: messages in the visitor\'s language, the current page, the persisted collapse', async () => {
  const storage = memoryStorage();
  storage.setItem('locale', 'de');
  storage.setItem('sn:nav-collapsed', 'true');
  const { root } = await firstPaint(page, { messages, storage });
  expect([...root.querySelectorAll('a')].map((a) => [a.textContent, a.getAttribute('aria-current')])).toEqual([['E-Mail', 'page'], ['Kalender', null]]);
  expect(root.querySelector('input')!.checked).toBe(true);
  expect(root.querySelector('nav > span')).toBeNull();  // the user's name waits for its data
});

test('the page module takes over without changing what was shown, then fills in data', async () => {
  const storage = memoryStorage();
  storage.setItem('sn:nav-collapsed', 'true');
  let shown = '';
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/user': { name: 'Ada' } });
  const { root, settle } = await render(page, {
    messages, storage, requests,
    firstPaint: { afterEarly: () => { shown = document.querySelector('nav')!.outerHTML; } },
  });
  expect(root.querySelector('nav')!.outerHTML).toBe(shown);
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('nav')!.textContent).toContain('Ada');
  expect(root.querySelector('input')!.checked).toBe(true);
});
```

### Messages: m.key() from the inlang files, switching without a reload

```html
<!-- Messages: m.key() from the inlang files (project.inlang, messages/{locale}.json), with {param}s.
     The build gives this page one small file per language with only the keys it calls; the language is
     picked before the first paint. $locale = … switches without a reload. -->
<body data-sn-state="{ lang: $locale }">
  <sn-resource name="inbox" src="/api/inbox" type="any"></sn-resource>
  <h1 data-sn-text="m.inbox_title()"></h1>
  <p data-sn-text="m.inbox_count({ count: inbox ? inbox.unread : 0 })"></p>
  <select data-sn-model="lang" data-sn-on-change="$locale = lang" data-sn-attr="{'aria-label': m.language()}">
    <option value="en">English</option>
    <option value="de">Deutsch</option>
  </select>
</body>
```

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { memoryStorage, mockRequests, render } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing';
import page from './messages.html?raw';

// messages/en.json and messages/de.json (the base language first)
const messages = {
  en: { inbox_title: 'Inbox', inbox_count: '{count} unread', language: 'Language' },
  de: { inbox_title: 'Posteingang', inbox_count: '{count} ungelesen', language: 'Sprache' },
};

test('the stored language, with parameters; switching re-renders without a reload', async () => {
  const storage = memoryStorage();
  storage.setItem('locale', 'de');
  const requests = mockRequests({ 'GET /api/inbox': { unread: 3 } });
  const { root, settle, flush, navigations } = await render(page, { messages, storage, requests });
  await settle();
  expect(root.querySelector('h1')!.textContent).toBe('Posteingang');
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toBe('3 ungelesen');

  const select = root.querySelector('select')!;
  select.value = 'en';
  select.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }));
  await flush();
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 0));
  await flush();
  expect(root.querySelector('h1')!.textContent).toBe('Inbox');
  expect(root.querySelector('p')!.textContent).toBe('3 unread');
  expect(document.documentElement.lang).toBe('en');
  expect(navigations).toEqual([]);
});
```

## Type checking

`npx sinter check` type-checks every expression with the project's TypeScript (pages and options come from the Vite config). `sinter({ typecheck: true })` runs it in `vite build`.

- `<sn-resource … type="Contact[]">`: the type of what `items` selects, using names exported by `src/sinter.types.ts`. `type="any"` opts out; no `type` is warning SN504.
- APIs: `sinter({ apis: { main: { base, openapi: 'openapi.yml', credentials, headers, defaults: { 'GET /articles': { items, total, key, type, query } }, operations: { … } } }, defaultApi })`. Pages write paths relative to an API: `src="/articles?tag={t}"`, `src="billing:/invoices"`, `data-sn-delete="/articles/{a.slug}"`, `src="site:/config.json"` (the page's own origin). Every path must be an operation the API declares (spec or `operations`) with the place's method (SN326), with declared and required query parameters, `paginate`'s included (SN327); an absolute URL is SN328. `items`/`total`/`key`/`type` come from `defaults`/`operations`: restating them is SN518 (same) or SN330 (different). `key` is never guessed: a list of objects without it is SN517. Each request carries its API's credentials and headers; `apiOf(url)` names the API in a middleware. `<sn-resource method="POST" body="{ q }">` loads with a POST (no cache, paginate, each). `npx sinter migrate --write` rewrites URLs into paths. Resources are typed from the operation's JSON response at `items`; every build checks `items`/`total` against the schema (SN308). Guide: docs/apis.md. The older `sinter({ openapi })` (deprecated) matches full `src` URLs and only warns (SN505).
- State takes a JSDoc cast where the literal is not enough: `data-sn-state="{ editing: /** @type {Contact|null} */ (null) }"`.
- Actions matched in the spec: `data-sn-body` is checked against the request schema, `$result` in `then` has the response type.
- `$result` in `<sn-resource then>` has the resource's type (`type`, OpenAPI, or a `call`'s result).
- `<sn-event … type="ContactEvent">` types the payload; `item` must fit the resource's item, `set` part of it, and `then` is checked against it; `cursor` reads the item. No `type` on an event with payload expressions is warning SN506.
- In the URL, body, call arguments and confirm of an element `run('id')` starts (not a form), `$event` is `RunEvent<…>` (no event when run): guard reads with `$event && $event.shiftKey`.
- SN509 (`run-cycle`) is opt-in: `sinter check --check-cycles`, or `sinter({ checkCycles: true })` for the build, `sinter check` and `sinter lsp`. It reports `then`/`catch` handlers that start each other again through `run()` (and `refresh()`), with every step.
- Errors are SN208 at the HTML position, with TypeScript's message. Null checks are off. In tests: `checkPage(html, { files, openapi })` from `@tiaforge-ui/sinter/check`; `render(html, { apis })` takes the APIs with parsed specs.

## First paint

The built page shows its chrome before the page module has run; the page bundle is not render-blocking and is `async` (it does not wait for stylesheets), so it may run while the body is still being parsed: keep app code at module top level from reading the body, and don't read an island's children or later siblings in `connectedCallback`. The page module waits for the parse and for the early script's last pass before it mounts.

- Build-time constants are written into the HTML: bindings outside templates that read only literal `data-sn-state` fields and constants (`aria-current` from `here === '/mail/'`). No helpers. A `data-sn-for` over a constant list (a literal, a prop given as one, state nothing writes) whose rows read only the item, its index and constants is unrolled at build time.
- A page with nothing left to run (no state anything writes, no data, `$url`, helpers, handlers, actions, models or component scripts) ships no JavaScript: no page module, no early script, its components' styles linked. The build prints `sinter: <page>: no JavaScript`, or what runs and where. `sinter({ static: ['about.html', 'docs/**'] | true })` lists pages that must stay that way: one that needs the runtime is SN322 where the cause was written. On such a page `src/sinter.config.ts` and `src/sinter.early.ts` do not run, and next-page data is not prefetched (Speculation Rules still are). Guide: docs/static-pages.md.
- Page URLs: every page without `data-sn-path` (not `index.html`, `404.html`, `200.html`) is a directory's index: `about.html` is `about/index.html` at `/about/`; `/about` redirects there on any static server, and `about.html` remains as a redirect (query and fragment kept). Links in the markup to a page, by its file or its URL, are written as its URL; a moved page's relative URLs are rebased. Links built at run time are not: write `'/task/?id=' + t.id`, not `'/task.html?id='` (a build warning). A page with `data-sn-path` answers at exactly its paths (absolute; patterns such as `/article/:slug`, `/ /tag/:tag`, or a fixed `/login` without a trailing slash) and stays in its file; a pattern also matches with a trailing slash; only its own directory URL is SN515. The build writes `_redirects` (Netlify, Cloudflare Pages; after `public/_redirects`; `sinter({ redirects: false })` turns it off): 301 for old file URLs, 200 rewrites for declared paths. `vite dev`, `vite preview` and sinter-axum follow the same rules; other servers: docs/static-pages.md#page-urls.
- Canonical URLs: `sinter({ site: 'https://example.com' })` (an origin; a path is Vite's `base`). `$site` is the origin and `base` (`https://example.com/docs`), `$canonical` the page's URL (`$site` and its path: `/guide/install/`); both are build-time constants on a page with a fixed path: `<meta property="og:url" data-sn-attr="{ content: $canonical }">`. Every such page gets `<link rel="canonical">`; a page's own canonical link must be absolute and is `$canonical`. On a pattern page `$canonical` and its canonical link are the origin and the browser's path, written by the early script (when the page ships JavaScript anyway). Without `site` either name is SN323.
- Languages in the URL: `sinter({ localePrefix: true })` with the built-in messages (`baseLocale` required, among `locales`) builds each page once per language under its prefix (`/en/about/`, `/de/about/`; the base too), `<html lang>` set, its messages and `$locale` written into the HTML (attributes too): no JavaScript for a page with nothing else to run. `localeUrl('de')` is this page's URL in German (`<a hreflang="de" data-sn-attr="{ href: localeUrl('de') }">`); assigning `$locale` is SN203. Links to your pages stay in the language; `<a hreflang>` is left alone. `data-sn-path` is written without the prefix; `$url` excludes it. With `site`: `hreflang` links and `x-default`. Unprefixed URLs are language choosers (the base language without JavaScript; with JavaScript on the site, the `locale` cookie pages with a script set, else the browser's languages); sinter-axum answers them with a 302. Guide: docs/static-pages.md#languages.
- Each page gets an early script: two classic scripts first in the head, before the stylesheets (one shared by every page with the early runtime and `src/sinter.early.ts`, then the page's own). Nothing holds the paint: a `MutationObserver` renders each binding as the parser inserts its element (an element's attributes at once, its content once the parser has closed it), before the browser can paint it, in every browser. It runs first `src/sinter.early.ts` (optional app code), then the bindings outside `data-sn-for` templates that need no data: they read state fields whose initial value needs no data, persisted values (read from `sn:<key>` in localStorage), `$locale` and helpers. A `data-sn-if` of that kind renders its branch; the page module adopts it. The compiler writes them as straight-line code calling only the writers they need; only the helpers and message members those bindings call are included. Other modules it shares with the page bundle are copies: state the early module sets must be set again by the page bundle (sinter's messages share theirs through a global).
- Resources, `$url`, `$now`, `$meta`, `$el`, loops and the built-in formatters (`date()`, …) wait for the page module. The runtime then owns every binding; its first write changes nothing.
- Every origin a literal `src` names (resources and streams) gets `<link rel="preconnect" crossorigin>`. Data requests start before the page module: a resource with a literal `src` and no `when` gets `<link rel="preload" as="fetch" crossorigin>`; one whose URL reads only state that needs no data, persisted values, `$now`, `$url` and helpers is requested by the early script as soon as it runs, before the stylesheets have loaded. Same-origin `src`, or an origin listed in `sinter({ origins: ['https://api.example.com'] })`, which every page also adds to the runtime's allowlist (list API origins there, not in `configure({ origins })`; cross-origin requests go without credentials); the build names the origins it left to the page module. `<sn-resource early="off">` keeps one resource out: one a request middleware answers itself or adds a header to (an `Authorization` token), whose early request would go unused. The runtime takes those responses at the end of its middleware chain when the request is unchanged (no header or credentials added), so response middleware still runs; changed requests are sent again. A paginated resource is requested at its first page, as the pager sends it (`size-param`=`page-size`, the `first` value of `direction-values` or `page-param`=1, no cursor), and `$meta` is as after any first load; with `cache` the cached page shows at once and the early response revalidates it. Not for `each`, `call` or embedded resources. A resource only elements inside `<dialog>`s read is requested with low priority (`fetchpriority="low"` on its preload, `priority: 'low'` on its fetch).
- Next-page data: when the pointer rests on a same-origin link to another page of the app (65 ms), it has focus, a mouse press starts on it, or a touch stays 65 ms without becoming a scroll, that page's resources whose `src`/`when` read only `$url`, constants and helpers are requested (low priority, through the middleware; data this page loaded from the same request is handed over without one). The next page shows them at once and revalidates; `$meta.<name>.loadedAt` stays null until the server answers. Entries are taken once, kept 30 s, dropped after any mutation; a failed prefetch never triggers `onUnauthorized`. Nothing to write: give pages `data-sn-path` patterns so links like `/article/slug` match. `sinter({ prefetch: false })` turns it off; test with `render(html, { pages: { 'article.html': articleHtml } })`. In Chromium, pages also get Speculation Rules for those links (`sinter({ speculation: 'prefetch' | 'prerender' | false })`, default `'prefetch'`); they are an inline script: a CSP in a `<meta>` gets their hash from the build; a nonce CSP via Vite's `html.cspNonce` needs nothing (Vite nonces the rules script); any other CSP sent as a response header needs `'inline-speculation-rules'` in `script-src` (dev builds warn), or use `speculation: { mode: 'prefetch', delivery: 'header' }` (the server sends `Speculation-Rules: "/speculation-rules.json"` and serves that file as `application/speculationrules+json`). Guide: docs/navigation.md. A prerendered page connects streams once shown and refetches then. A page that does something when it loads (logout) gets `<html data-sn-prefetch="off">`: no page prefetches or prerenders it. Page transitions: with `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` in the CSS (temper has it), `data-sn-transition="'article-' + a.slug"` on an element of a list row and `data-sn-transition="'article-' + $url.slug"` on the detail page morph one into the other when the row's link is followed (and back). Use one name per thing; the detail element must render with the page (not after a later load).
- Same-page links: a plain click on a link to the page itself that changes only query parameters the page reads (`$url.<name>`) stays on the page: a new history entry, `$url` takes the link's query, and the page shows what loading the URL would (a `page-model` list loads the link's page; `?tag=js&page=3` shows page 3). Not for another path, `download`, a `target`, `rel="external"`, modifier keys, or a parameter the page does not read: those load. Loaded (`@tiaforge-ui/sinter/query-links`) only on pages with a link the build sees goes to the page (a static `href`, or a `data-sn-attr` `href` that starts with the page's path or `?`). Build the whole query: `href="?page=3"` drops the other parameters (SN519). Guide: docs/navigation.md#same-page-links.
- Embedded data renders early too: a resource with `<script type="application/json" data-sn-data="name">` in the head (filled by a server or middleware) is read by the early script, which renders the bindings over it, `data-sn-for` rows included, as the parser goes; the page module adopts the rows. A middleware that fetches the API and writes the JSON in is enough for data in the first frame: no server rendering.
- Server layer for JavaScript: `sinter({ embed: true })` writes `dist/sinter-embed.json` (and its types, `sinter-embed.d.ts`); `import { embed } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/server'`, then `const sinter = await embed<Build>({ dir: 'dist', data: { user: 'skip', 'profile.html:articles': (req) => … } })` and `export default { fetch: sinter.wrap(app.fetch) }` (Hono, Bun.serve, Deno.serve, Workers; on Node, through `@hono/node-server` or `srvx`). It streams each page head first and fills the slots from the wrapped app called in-process (cookies forwarded), `upstream`, `origins` or a resolver (returns a value, a JSON text, bytes or a `Response`; null leaves it to the browser). A slot whose request the build cannot describe needs an entry in `data`: a type error with `embed<Build>`, an error at startup without. docs/server.md
- Google Fonts: a `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/…">` is downloaded at build time and bundled as one of the app's CSS files (no inline style: no CSP change), with a preconnect to the font files' origin; the fonts and the look stay the same, one render-blocking request to another origin less. Cached in `node_modules/.cache/sinter/fonts`; a build that cannot download it keeps the link and warns. `sinter({ fonts: { inline: false } })` turns it off.
- Heavy packages: `sinter({ lazy: ['openpgp'] })` loads a package on first call. App code imports it as usual; the build points those imports at stubs sharing one `import()` (the package is a chunk of its own). Every call of its exports must be waited for (`await`, `return`, `.then`, `void`, `Promise.all`); `new`, `instanceof`, constants, settings, functions passed as values, side-effect imports and re-exports are SN324, and so is a helpers module that reaches it. A component script that imports it (directly or through app modules) loads with it when its component first renders; any use is fine there. `data-sn-import="openpgp"` on an element loads it when the element renders (never before takeover); `data-sn-preload="openpgp"` adds modulepreload links to the page's head. SN325: a page bundle that contains it through another package, or that imports statically a module it also loads with `import()`. A chunk a deploy removed gives `$error.stale = true` (`status: 0` is the network). docs/lazy.md.
- The build prints each page's early file size (gzip) and warns over `sinter({ earlyBudget })` (default 10000 bytes), naming the largest modules: keep heavy imports out of early code.
- Keep page chrome outside data templates: `<template data-sn-if="user">` around the navigation hides it until the user has loaded.
- `sinter({ firstPaint: false })` turns it off. Test with `firstPaint(html, { helpers, storage, early })` from the testing module (`early` stands for `src/sinter.early.ts`), and `render(html, { firstPaint: { early, afterEarly } })` for the takeover.

## Images

Write plain `<img src="./photo.jpg" alt="…">` (a local JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF, relative to the page or component): the build makes it a `<picture>` with AVIF (photos) or lossless WebP (PNG graphics), widths for every screen, `width`/`height`, `decoding="async"` and `loading="lazy"` (not on the page's first image), and the image's dominant color as background until it loads. Needs sharp (an optional dependency); `sinter({ images: false })` turns it off. See docs/images.md.

- No `width`/`height`, or the source's own: fluid. `sizes` is the image's width at every viewport width, from the CSS: per breakpoint of its width media queries, linear in the viewport, through grids (equal tracks, gaps, `span`, `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(…, 1fr))`), flex rows (equal `flex: 1` columns, wrapped items with a basis), max-width containers, margins and padding. When the CSS cannot be followed (`em`, `vh`, unequal tracks, `:hover`), the narrowest container with a fixed or absolute max width bounds it; write `sizes` yourself only then.
- `width`/`height` smaller than the source: a box of that size in CSS px, with 1x/2x(/3x) files of exactly that width. A source with too few pixels for 2x is SN511.
- A fixed width from the page's stylesheets (CSS, Sass, Less or Stylus, after the project's PostCSS; Tailwind and UnoCSS utilities the page uses, such as `size-12`; px, rem, calc and custom properties, % of a fixed parent; not media queries or states) is a box too, cropped when they say `object-fit: cover`: an `<img>` in temper's `[data-avatar]` needs no attributes. When they set a width that is not fixed (`width: 100%`), the image is fluid whatever its attributes.
- Images from the API: with `sinter({ images: { remote: { url: 'https://img.example.com/{w}/{url}', origins: ['self', 'https://uploads.example.com'] } } })` (or a preset: `cloudflare`, `vercel`, `netlify`, `imgproxy:<base>`), `<img data-sn-attr="{src: c.avatar}">` gets a `srcset` of the service's URLs, sized from the stylesheets like a static image. Write the binding as usual; only allowed origins go through the service. `cover` (a template with `{h}`) crops boxes with `object-fit: cover`. Tests: `render(html, { remoteImages, css })`.
- CSS backgrounds: write `background: url(./hero.jpg) center / cover` as usual; the build adds `image-set()` with AVIF/WebP and 1x/2x files (the source counts as 2x when the rule sizes the background, else 1x only). Use a source twice the largest width the background is shown at.
- Dev: the console warns when an image or a CSS background is shown with fewer pixels than the screen has (a small source, or a `sizes` smaller than the image is shown).
- To crop: `width` and `height` of the box plus `style="object-fit: cover"` (and `object-position` for the part to keep); the build makes the cropped file and removes the inline style. Another ratio without `object-fit` is SN512 (stretched).
- Left as written: remote URLs, SVG, GIF, an `<img>` with `srcset`, inside your own `<picture>`, or with `data-sn-*` bindings.

## Messages

- With an inlang project (`project.inlang/settings.json`, message files `messages/{locale}.json` of plain `"key": "text with {param}"`), `m.key()` / `m.key({ param })` in markup are sinter's built-in messages. App code: `import { m } from '@tiaforge-ui/sinter/messages'`, typed by the generated `src/sinter.messages.d.ts`. Unknown keys are SN206, wrong or missing params SN208 (`sinter check`). Only `m.key`: `m[key]` or passing `m` on fails the build; a dynamic choice is a switch.
- The build emits one file per page and language with only the keys the page calls (markup and its modules); a missing translation is the base language, reported at build. No plurals or variants.
- Before the first paint the head script picks the language (localStorage `locale`, else `navigator.languages`, else the base), sets `<html lang>` and starts the page's language file without waiting for it; the base language's text is in the HTML, hidden for other languages until rendered (3 s at most): on every page that calls `m`, in its markup or in a helper, action or island it bundles. `$locale = 'de'` switches without a reload (stores the choice, loads that file, re-renders). Don't `configure({ locale })`: sinter is the locale source.
- Tests: `render(html, { messages: { en: {…}, de: {…} }, locale })`. An app without an inlang project ships none of this.

## Deploying streams

Each open EventSource holds one HTTP connection, and HTTP/1.1 allows 6 per origin: with more than 5 tabs open, pages stop loading. Serve streams over HTTP/2 (any TLS reverse proxy such as nginx or Caddy) or use the WebSocket transport; dev builds warn about HTTP/1.1.

## Editors

`npx sinter lsp --stdio` is a language server for the project's HTML files: sinter's diagnostics as you type (components checked through the pages that use them), and with TypeScript 7 type errors, hover, completion in expressions, go to definition and a did-you-mean quick fix; "Extract to helper" moves an expression into a typed function of the helpers module. VS Code: the extension in `editors/vscode`. Setup for Neovim, Helix and Emacs: `docs/editors.md`. Every diagnostic links to its explanation in `docs/diagnostics.md`.

## Testing

Write a test next to the markup. `@tiaforge-ui/sinter/testing` compiles the page with the real compiler and mounts it:

- `render(html, { requests, streams, url, locale, now, helpers, actions, files, components, layouts, scripts, storage, session, firstPaint })` → `{ root, app, state, flush, settle, advance, navigations, window }`. The page is compiled as a build compiles it (build-time constants, decided branches, unrolled loops). `state(el).update(fn)` writes the scope around `el` and re-renders it; it throws for a field nothing on the page writes, which the build made a constant (write it from a handler instead). Pass one `memoryStorage()` as `session` to two renders to test what carries over between page loads (the `cache` attribute). A full document keeps its `<html>` attributes, so state and `data-sn-persist` on `<html>` work as in the browser.
- `mockRequests({ 'GET /api/x': json | {status, body} | (call) => … })`: records `calls`; responses are held until `settle()`; an unmatched request fails the test and lists the routes.
- `mockStream()`: `emit(name, payload)`, `drop()`, `connected`. A stream URL with no mock uses the transport from `configure({ transport })`, so a custom transport can be tested over a fake connection (see the SignalR recipe).
- `flush()` runs the scheduler (optimistic changes are visible), `settle()` finishes requests, queues and debounces, `advance(ms)` moves sinter's clock.
- `firstPaint(html, { helpers, files, storage, early })` → `{ root, html }`: the page as the browser shows it before the page module runs (build-time constants, then the early chunk). `render(…, { firstPaint: { early, afterEarly } })` mounts over that first paint; `afterEarly` runs in between, so a test can watch what mounting changes.
